preparation.description: Durable preparation state for the run's preparation axis. This is an operational summary only; it never exposes connector-owned preparation input. It is not nullable: admission creates a run, its preparation, and its execution in one transaction and nothing deletes an axis on its own, so every readable run carries a summary. A row whose preparation is missing is corrupt — Review Runs drops it from list reads and answers 404 for a single-run read, logging the fault — rather than reported with a null summary.

status.description: Preparation lifecycle. `preparing` means a preparer currently owns the claim; it is the preparation axis's own "in progress" state and is unrelated to the Execution API provider, which is only submitted to once preparation reaches `submitted`.

disconnect_reason.description: Non-null only while `status` is `disconnected`: the reason the run's own records do not admit the transition an expired lease would make, so automatic work cannot conclude it. It names that conflict and nothing else - what an operator may do about it is the `disconnected` state's business, not this field's. The value today is `EXECUTION_ALREADY_ADVANCED`.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the preparation phase began (a preparer first claimed the work); null while it is still pending. A retry that returns the row to pending and claims it again does not move it, so it is a safe start bound for the phase.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the preparation phase reached a terminal state (`submitted` or `failed`); null while it is pending or preparing. Distinct from `updated_at`, which also moves on claim heartbeats and input checkpoints and cannot mark the phase end.

updated_at.description: Last time the preparation axis was written, including claim heartbeats and input checkpoints. This is the activity freshness the console reports, not a phase bound — use `started_at` and `finished_at` for that. A preparation that is still being built keeps advancing here even though its bounds do not.

status.description: The execution lifecycle as coordinated through Execution API provider. `pending` means the run has been admitted but its prepared input has not yet been submitted to the Execution API provider; preparation progress is reported separately by `preparation`. `skipped` means execution never ran because preparation failed; the reason is on `preparation`, not here. `uncertain` means a submission may have reached the Execution API provider but its result could not be confirmed; a recovery replays it under the same identity. `disconnected` means automatic recovery stopped after its finite budget without a conclusive answer, so it is not a failure.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the prepared Execution input was accepted and execution began; null while the run is still pending, and also null for `skipped`, which is concluded without ever having started. Written once, so a recovery replay does not move it.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the execution axis reached a terminal state (`succeeded`, `failed`, or `skipped`); null while it is pending, queued, running, uncertain, or disconnected. Together with `started_at` it times the phase (only when `started_at` is non-null, since `skipped` has an end without a start).

updated_at.description: Last time the execution axis was written: a polling confirmation, a state transition, or a submission/recovery write. This is the observation freshness the console reports ("observed Ns ago"), not a phase bound — use `started_at` and `finished_at` for that.

started_at.description: Immutable instant the publication phase began (the work was first claimed); null while it is pending, and null for `skipped`, which is concluded without ever having started. A retryable failure that returns the row to pending and claims it again does not move it.

finished_at.description: Immutable instant the publication axis reached a terminal state (`published`, `failed`, or `skipped`); null while it is pending or publishing. It is set for every terminal outcome. The instant the result became visible is this field read together with `status: published`.

updated_at.description: Last time the publication axis was written, including claim heartbeats. This is the activity freshness the console reports, not a phase bound — use `started_at` and `finished_at` for that. Unlike them it keeps advancing while a long publication runs.

notices.description: User-visible notices caused by this run's coordination events, in creation order.

items.description: Delivery state of one user-visible coordination notice.

comment_url.description: Where the requester can read the outcome. Always an absolute URI when present, and null only when no message reached them.
